social_circle.name: Marta Tangarife

demographics.occupation: retired school cafeteria worker and occasional church volunteer

background.how_they_met: Marta is Irene's younger sister; they grew up together in a bilingual Salvadoran American household in southwest Houston.
background.why_close: They share childhood memories, Catholic family traditions, health concerns, and a long habit of helping each other through worry and practical problems.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts in short Spanish-English sentences, often with practical reminders. She sometimes sends voice notes when the story is too long to type.

shared_activities: phone calls about family, church, and health
occasional visits on the southwest side of Houston
recent_text_topics: Marta reminding Irene, 'One thing at a time,' when Irene worries about bills, blood pressure, or family stress.
Coordinating rides or check-ins around Marta's diabetes concerns and doctor appointments.
Family news, church events, and old stories about their parents.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q06 explicitly names Marta as Irene's sister: 'We talk by phone several times a week.' Q44 says Irene called Marta during a rough week, and Q35 says Irene worries about her sister's diabetes concerns.

social_circle.name: Ana Morales

demographics.education: some community college and medical office training

background.how_they_met: Ana is Irene's adult daughter, raised by Irene in Houston after Irene's marriage and later divorce.
background.why_close: Ana is the child Irene turns to for a second set of ears about prescriptions and online health information, and she is part of the nearby Houston family network.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Uses clear, efficient texts with calendar details, screenshots, and reminders. She answers quickly during breaks at work and uses WhatsApp for family group planning.

recent_text_topics: Checking whether vaccine or health information Irene saw online was reliable.
Clarifying prescription instructions after Irene asked the pharmacist questions.
Coordinating grandchildren's visits, food, and school pickup help.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Ana is inferred as Irene's daughter from Q39, where Irene says the pharmacist and 'sometimes my daughter' help her understand prescriptions. Q42 says Irene asks her children to verify online health information. Q05 and Q51 establish Irene has grown children with their own Houston-area households.

social_circle.name: Rafael Morales

demographics.education: high school diploma and trade certification

background.how_they_met: Rafael is Irene's adult son, one of her grown children living in the broader Houston area.
background.why_close: He is part of Irene's practical family support network, especially around home repairs, storm preparation, and grandchildren's schedules.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts briefly and practically, often with 'Ok Ma' or a photo of something he fixed. He is more likely to respond with a call if Irene seems worried.

shared_activities: family meals with pupusas or tamales
recent_text_topics: Whether Irene's air conditioner was holding up in the Houston heat.
Plans for a family birthday meal at Irene's house.
Reminders about car maintenance, tires, and storm supplies.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Rafael is inferred as one of Irene's grown children from Q05 and Q51. Q62 says air conditioning is the home repair that worries Irene most, Q82 says she expects car or air conditioning repair emergencies, and Q46 says Irene supports her children with food, listening, childcare, and reminders to rest.

social_circle.name: Lucia Morales

background.how_they_met: Lucia is one of Irene's grandchildren who visits Irene's home on weekends and school breaks.
background.why_close: Irene is deeply involved with her grandchildren through food, stories, cultural events, Spanish prayers, and occasional after-school help.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Texts with short phrases, photos, reaction emojis, and TikTok-style links. She sometimes sends voice memos asking 'Abuela, can you make tamales?'

recent_text_topics: Sending Irene funny videos and explaining TikTok jokes Irene does not fully understand.
Asking whether Irene is making pupusas, tamales, beans, or quesadillas when she visits.
Sharing school updates, art club pictures, and family birthday plans.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Lucia is inferred as one of Irene's grandchildren from Q05, Q13, and Q19. Q48 says Irene does not understand TikTok except when grandchildren show her funny videos; Q19 mentions one grandchild likes art club; Q05 says grandchildren come over for pupusas or tamales.

social_circle.name: Celia Ramirez

demographics.education: high school diploma plus early childhood education certificates

background.how_they_met: Celia and Irene met while teaching together years ago in early childhood classrooms.
background.why_close: They stayed close after working together because they share teaching memories, bilingual classroom experience, Catholic and family values, and the habit of checking on each other.

personality_mini_profile.communication_style: Writes full, friendly texts with greetings and blessings. She forwards church event details and asks direct questions about Irene's health.

shared_activities: checking in about health and family
recent_text_topics: Scheduling their next coffee visit around Irene's workdays and knee pain.
Talking about younger teachers, classroom routines, and Irene's idea for a Salvadoran preschool guide.
Checking on Irene after blood pressure worries and asking whether she is resting enough.
social_circle.evidence_from_interview: Q07 explicitly names Celia as a former coworker and one of Irene's closest friends: 'Celia, who taught with me years ago, is still one of my closest friends, and we meet for coffee maybe once a month.' Q03 says Irene talked over the divorce-era work decision with Marta and 'one teacher friend named Celia.'
